newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom result reflects abnormals, Pac Star.
newsitem.headline: Telecom result reflects abnormals, Pac Star.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand on Wednesday reported a net profit of NZ$581.4 million for the year ended March 31 compared with $716.8 last year.
Telecom said the reported earnings for 1997 reflected abnormal costs of $101.5 million after tax and the losses of Australian subsidiary Pacific Star, which amounted to NZ$87.6 million.
* costs of $43.2 million after tax associated with Telecom's ongoing restructuring programme,
* the cost of "future-proofing", or making millennium compliant, the company's computer systems to cope with the year 2000, totalling $58.3 million after tax,

* operating losses for Pacific Star of $50.2 million for the year, plus a further provision of $37.4 million, comprising further losses expected to arise and the costs related to the sale or winding down of the business.
Normalised earnings, excluding the effect of abnormals and Pacific Star, were $770.5 million compared with $746.4 million in 1996, an increase of 3.2 percent, Telecom said.
Net earnings for 1997 also reflected the start-up costs associated with Telecom's internet venture Xtra and cable tv operation First Media.
"Excluding start-up costs associated with Telecom's entry into those new business oportunities, normalised net earnings would have increased by $41.7 million, or 5.5 percent, for 1997," Telecom said.

Reported earnings for the fourth quarter were $53.3 million while normalised earnings were $202 million, a decrease of $12.6 million or 5.8 percent compared with the same quarter last year, excluding the effect of Pacific Star.
"The result for the fourth quarter 1997 includes a one-off depreciation charge of $14.5 million and a further $5 million adjustment to cellular revenue," Telecom said.
It said excluding those one-off items and the abnormal costs, fourth quarter earnings would have approximated the fourth quarter earnings of last year.
Chief executive Roderick Deane said volume growth remained strong in many areas, particularly enhanced network services, with a particular highlight being 0800 revenue rising 56 percent.
He said continued rapid declines in prices for national and international calls were being partially offset by double-digit percentage volume increases.
Cellular connections now totalled well over 400,000, up 24.5 percent on last year, and at 14 percent, penetration offered considerable potential over coming years.
Chairman Peter Shirtcliffe said it was pleasing to see revenue growth at 6.2 percent, well above economic growth rates, and despite the significant price falls customers were enjoying.
Telecom confirmed the second stage of its year-long $1 billion share repurchase would start shortly. It had purchased nearly 55 million shares for more than $350 million in February and March.

Telecom had also established a value of $2.6 billion for its brands but because of the current international uncertainty regarding accounting standards in this area, this figure was only recognised in supplementary financial information rather than being incorporated into its main balance sheet.
